assessment: This study finds that voltage-gated calcium channel auxiliary β2a and β2e splice variants confer gating properties on Cav2.3 channels that enable them to contribute sustained Ca2+ influx during pacemaking in substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons. This sustained Ca2+ influx may contribute to the selective vulnerability of substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons to neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease. The work will be of great interest to ion channel biophysicists and neuroscientists interested in mechanisms of neurodegeneration.
